summary: One cold read (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only, task-mtx978cr-so0jqv) against plans/drafts/drill-down.md returned NOT CONVERGED with eight blocking findings. Five were answered by the repository and resolved directly; three were put to the human in one AskUserQuestion round and the plan was amended once to what they decided. Decisions 0024 and 0025 were accepted in the same round. The plan was then amended a second time by the requirements re-read that followed (the two accepted decisions staled the requirements pass); those amendments are recorded in the requirements grill and listed below.
gaps: unmapped-GL cannot pass the stated node-key rule: the statement synthesises it outside the outline snapshot (mis-statement.service.ts:199), so 'reject any nodeKey absent from the outline' contradicts acceptance criterion 5.
Grand Total has no descendants to flatten: it is a separate MisStatementNode with children: [] while the roots live in response.tree, so a generic client-side flatten yields an empty panel.

The FY-YTD multi-batch footing proof has no data source: the supplied SAP extract contains July only (docs/context/2026-08-20-srihari-phase1-data/README.md), so 'foots across several monthly batches' cannot be demonstrated against client data.
The API contract was underspecified: no route path, page base/size/maximum, invalid-page behaviour, stale-snapshot response, or typed 400/401/403 Swagger coverage as decision 0019 requires.
Posting date is required by the spec's line-item column list but absent from the approved prototype's six-column drill table, and the plan assigned it to no rendered surface.
contradictions: The audit sequence as written was impossible: criterion 9 demanded the full-predicate audit record before ANY warehouse read, but the resolver (selection-resolver.service.ts) and outline repository (statement-outline.repository.ts) must both read the warehouse before the predicate the record names can exist.

'Valid actual batch ids in range' does not preserve footing: a client that omits one month's batch from an FY-YTD pin only narrows the read, which is safe for authorization but produces a footer that silently disagrees with the number clicked. The plan claimed narrowing made acceptance safe without qualifying that claim to authorization.
Decisions 0024 and 0025 were listed in decisions_reviewed and depended on throughout while their records still read status: proposed.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED — unmapped-GL is now specified as a RESERVED node key: acceptance criterion 5 and the predicate table state that it maps to the reserved leaf key 'unmapped-GL' whose triples are the resolver's leafTargets with target.kind === 'bucket'; the rejection rule now applies to every key that is neither a snapshot leaf nor that reserved key, and the risk bullet was corrected to match.

REPO-ANSWERED — acceptance criterion 3 now states the Grand Total special case explicitly (flatten the roots of response.tree, which already include the synthetic unmapped-GL root) and task 2 owns it in the decomposition.

REPO-ANSWERED — criterion 9 now reads 'before any sap_transaction read', states why the predicate-deriving resolver and outline lookups must precede the audit write, notes they read only mapping and outline metadata (the same lookups the shipped statement route makes), and the audit test now asserts that sap_transaction was never queried rather than that no warehouse query occurred.

REPO-ANSWERED — the Technical Approach now fixes the contract: POST api/mis/statement/drill, unversioned and raw per 0019, inheriting the global CsrfGuard registered in app.module.ts plus AuthGuard and RequireAction('report'); a 1-based page with a server-fixed page size of 100 that is not client-settable; and typed 400 / 401 / 403 / 409 responses declared with @ApiResponse alongside the success schema, mirroring mis-statement.controller.ts.

REPO-ANSWERED — the Verify Plan now states plainly that the client extract is July-only, that criteria 4 and 11 therefore CANNOT be proven against client data, and that the DB-backed suite constructs a deliberate multi-period actuals fixture for them; evidence labels which proofs rest on client data and which on the fixture. Task 1 owns the fixture.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) — batch binding: the server requires a COMPLETE month-for-month pinned set. It computes which months in the block's range have an actuals batch and requires exactly one pinned id per such month; a missing month is refused as a stale snapshot (new acceptance criterion 11), an id that is not an actuals batch for its month is a 400, an id that is valid but no longer active means replaced (read the pin, say so), and an id that no longer exists is reported as gone and refused. A wrong footer becomes unrepresentable. Rejected: a server-held snapshot token (new server state and a change to the statement route this story otherwise leaves alone) and server-side recomputation (drops the pin the requirements grill mandated).

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) — Posting date is rendered as a seventh column in the transactions table, in the prototype's own styling. The plan records this as a deliberate, reasoned departure from the approved design: the spec's column list is normative, posting date is what a finance user cross-checks against SAP (a line's month is its booking month), and the prototype predates the settled tie-break that also uses posting date. Task 3 owns it.

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) — decisions 0024 and 0025 were confirmed in chat and accepted: forge decision accept --by 'kl-rahulanand' on both, and both now read status: accepted and appear in forge decision list --active. The plan's Decisions section records them as accepted 2026-09-11 rather than proposed.

CARRIED FROM THE REQUIREMENTS RE-READ — the plan was amended again to add the budget-batch pin (the outline snapshot that maps nodeKey to leaf is is_active-filtered, so a budget re-upload would break footing with every actuals id correct), the typed drill audit event with refused attempts audited, the rupee footer with an exact-paise secondary line, the empty-result success case, and the resulting Surface Impact and decomposition updates. Acceptance criteria now run to fifteen.
open_items: Non-blocking — the statement and export routes still write no audit event (AuditService.writeRequestEvent has exactly one caller, chat.service.ts:317). Ledgered as D-0036 with its revisit trigger rather than widened into this story.

Non-blocking — ORDER BY (debit - credit) DESC has no supporting index. Carried as a named risk with an EXPLAIN check against the real July batch in the DB-backed suite, rather than a speculative index in this story.

rounds.question: The drill pins to batch ids the browser sends. The grill found a real hole: `provenance.activeBatchIds` is statement-wide (both sources, all blocks), so a client that omits one month's actuals batch from an FY-YTD drill narrows the read and produces a footer that silently disagrees with the number clicked. Authorization is still safe — omitting only ever reads less — but footing is not. How should the server bind the pinned set?
options: Server recomputes and ignores the client's list

rounds.question: Column conflict the grill caught: the spec's Behaviour section lists line items as 'Month, Debit, Credit, Value, reference, memo, posting date', but the approved prototype's drill table has six columns and no posting date. Posting date is also part of the settled deterministic tie-break, so it exists in the data either way.
options: Show it, but only on the row detail

rounds.question: The plan depends on two decisions I minted while planning; both are `proposed` and need your confirmation before the plan can honestly claim to reconcile with the active corpus. 0024 — the aggregate drill is a client-side projection of the statement payload, so only leaf→transactions crosses the network. 0025 — the transaction drill reads sap_transaction directly under a pinned batch_id predicate, beside the governed executor but reusing its authorization/validator/explain/timeout, with a pre-query fail-closed audit.
options: Hold both — I want to read them first

rounds.question: Closing the plan grill. Eight findings: five the repo answered (reserved `unmapped-GL` key; Grand Total flattens `response.tree` roots; audit boundary is 'before any sap_transaction read'; route/page/error contract pinned to house style; FY-YTD proof needs a constructed multi-period fixture because the client extract is July-only), three you settled (complete month-for-month pin, Posting date as a 7th column, both decisions accepted). The plan is amended and the two decisions are accepted. Any remaining gap before this hands off to decomposition?
